title: Flexible On-Prem Support Bands with Predictable Upgrade Windows
creator: Samantha Ortiz
description: Run a time-boxed experiment to validate a flexible, tiered support and entitlement model for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that pairs (1) annual license fee bands, (2) optional paid emergency SLA add-ons, and (3) predictable upgrade windows for security/critical patches. Goals: reduce sales friction on enterprise contracts, make upgrade cadence deterministic for engineering, and streamline Security Questionnaire (SQ) responses mapping to each support band. Deliverables include pricing bands, example contract clauses, support playbooks for each band, a draft SQ response matrix, and pilot agreements for 3 qualified accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document three distinct license/support bands (Standard, Enhanced, Critical) with clear entitlements and example pricing ranges
Map a deterministic upgrade cadence for each band (major, minor, emergency) and agree SLOs/response times with Eng leads
Complete a security questionnaire matrix for each band and validate with one Security & Legal review
Secure verbal pilot commitments from at least 3 customers and convert 1 pilot into an MSA amendment or purchase order
Produce a concise PRD and two example contract appendix templates for sales/legal review
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Sales Engineering, Security, and Legal. Agreed scope: pricing bands + upgrade cadence + SQ mapping. Action: PM to draft band definitions (Samantha).

2026-03-06: Internal tech review with Elena Park (Infra) and Marco Liu (SRE). Confirmed feasibility of staggered upgrade windows and emergency hotfix path. Engineering requested explicit rollback SLAs for Critical band.
2026-03-09: Draft pricing ranges shared with GTM; received market feedback that seatless commit option should be included. Added to scope.

2026-03-11: Security ran initial SQ mapping; existing questions around data residency and KMS key custody flagged for Critical band. Security suggested templated answers and optional onsite audit option.
2026-03-13: PRD v0.3 published (link below). Sales identified two enterprise accounts for pilots; Account Execs assigned. Legal requested standardized indemnity language for emergency patching.
2026-03-15: Decision: proceed with three-band model and pilot outreach; next step pilot contracts (Rahul) and engineering runbook for upgrade windows (ENG owners).
notes: Trade-offs: wider bands reduce negotiation friction but increase risk of underpriced support for high-incident customers.
Risk: Customers on Standard band may push emergency fixes outside agreed windows, need clear contractual penalties or uplift paths.
Operational impact: Engineering must automate patch orchestration and maintain dedicated runbooks per band; estimate 2 sprint effort from infra team for rollout automation.
Mitigation: Include explicit escalation ladder and paid emergency SLA add-on that covers rollback and on-call engineering time for Critical customers.
